title: NINT rounding: most compilers ship half-to-even; Java Math.round is half-up
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE ROUND_TO_INT(X, R)
C     NINT is the standard Fortran nearest-integer intrinsic. The
C     F77/F90 standard is unspecified on midpoints (0.5, -0.5,
C     1.5...): most modern compilers ship IEEE round-half-to-even
C     (banker's rounding), but legacy IBM XL Fortran shipped
C     half-away-from-zero. Reading code that called NINT and
C     translating it to Java's Math.round (half-up) silently
C     diverges on tied inputs.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL X
      INTEGER R
      R = NINT(X)
      RETURN
      END
notes: NINT's tie-breaking is the most under-documented Fortran-to-Java porting gotcha. Statistical-software migrations that match historical results to the cent depend on knowing the original compiler's rounding mode. The spec must surface this AND ask the SME to confirm — a hand-port that picks 'round-half-up' silently breaks the equivalence test on every 0.5 input.
